purpose: Frozen implementation and evaluation of public-residual analytic-energy greedy phase pruning under a logical gate budget.
selection: Repeatedly remove the edge producing the lowest exact p=1 expectation of the full original cost at the frozen anchor angles. At each budget use magnitude pruning if its expectation is no worse. No enumerated costs, optima or secrets enter selection.
geometry_ablation: Run the same selector with residual r=0 and its own geometry-only normalization, then use only its edge mask with the real h,J. This mask depends only on the reduced basis.
training: Freeze masks using anchor angles on16 original separate training groups; fit one global angle pair per policy with equal768-evaluation budget on original energy. Freeze fits before all64 development and128 new groups are evaluated.
equal_effort_control: At K24, optimize ordinary-magnitude angles per instance using at most the residual selector analytic-call count, including initial trained anchor. Count both calls and wall time; these are not guaranteed equal CPU costs.
primary_comparison: On128 fresh groups, residual24 with global trained angles versus magnitude24 with independently globally trained angles, hybrid optimum success at1024 shots; paired two-sided95% bootstrap interval. Primary improvement supported only if lower bound>0. All other comparisons secondary/exploratory.
routing: Local compilation on frozen16-qubit Fez patch for primary trained full/residual24/magnitude24/geometry24; ideal circuit equality checks on first2 cases of each cohort. No noise simulation or QPU submission.
limitations: Logical RZZ cap is not a native CZ or runtime cap; routing is reported separately.
Optimizing expected energy need not improve rare optimum probabilities or secret recovery.
128 new groups are one small same-distribution validation, not scaling or secure ML-KEM.
Selection adds classical work and uses a p=1 analytic formula; no quantum advantage or algorithmic novelty claim.
Single routing seed and saved calibration; no new noise or hardware measurements.
